$comment: Design-quality baseline for scripts/check-design-quality.mjs. `waivers` are accepted on purpose and each names the check that covers the same risk. `outstanding` is the work left to do; it may only shrink without a commit that explains why it grew.

waivers.reason: NASA's composite display tokens declare 100% leading (--hds-typography-h1-2xl: 700 7.5rem/1, --hds-typography-number-lg: 300 7.5rem/1), which the detector divides as 1/7.5 and reports as 0.13x. Those tokens are vendored verbatim from data/design/nasa-hds/tokens.json (CC0-1.0) by scripts/import_nasa_tokens.mjs and must not be edited; --hds-line-height-1 documents 100% as NASA's own choice for h1, h2 display and numbers. Compensated by __tests__/designTypography.test.js, which requires >=1.3 leading on every body-scale rule in frontend/src/index.css and in the prerendered static shell, requires any tighter leading in the vendored token file to be a --hds-* declaration rather than an applied style, and forbids tight Tailwind leading on elements that wrap unless they are display scale or cannot wrap.

The detector converts the print stylesheet's `h1 { font-size: 18pt !important }` as though pt were rem and reports a 288px heading on every page that carries the print sheet. On screen the h1 is 28px, rising to 32px at 640px, per frontend/src/index.css. Compensated by __tests__/designTypography.test.js, which fails if a point size appears outside @media print or the paper-emulation scopes (.pdf-capture-mode, .print-preview-rendered-body, .print-*) and if any screen h1 exceeds NASA's 3rem/48px h1 ceiling.
